(2007–2018)… acquired by Brandwatch in 2018': the analytics firm is composed as part of the poem's lineage, as the node states it. Point 2 takes the Fractal Navigation Map v7.0 (#30, the Medium card): 'When you seek the actual text instead of summarizing — when you describe the mass rather than the content'; and its symbolon, 'half of a token broken in two'. In #30 describing the mass is the reader's act against summarizing; the Overview gives it as 'instructing or observing the processor to describe the mass'. 'Metafictional text' is the composer's label; #269 calls itself meta-documentation.

1. Start at the Summary ("The Doorway"): When an AI summarizer attempts to extract the "meaning" of the distributed epic, the generated summary serves as your primary threshold or entryway into the text.
2. Describe Mass over Content: You complete the reading loop ("the token") not by passively receiving distilled meanings, but by instructing or observing the processor to describe the mass and structural presence of the text.
3. Recognize the Retrocausal Lineage: Reading the text requires understanding its dual nature: it bridges Jorge Luis Borges’s fictional "crimson hexagon" (the ultimate, missing index room of the infinite Library of Babel) and the digital ghost of the real-world, defunct social analytics firm Crimson Hexagon Inc. (which was acquired by Brandwatch in 2018).

The summarizer is not just a tool explaining the text—it is a functional environment where the "distributed epic" performs its narrative.
